title: Enlightened arts, not magic
summary: How Daedaleans understand their own wonders.

claims.text: Daedaleans treat art, philosophy, science and scholarship as one field, where music and mathematics share the same rhythms.

The Order of Reason claims no link to magic; its members see nothing supernatural in their work, count themselves people using reason given by God, and believe they are trained to shield humanity from the occult.
Results beyond the ordinary are put down to mastery of a craft rather than sorcery.

title: Daedalean lodges
summary: The houses where cabals of the Order live and work.

claims.text: The Order runs schools, forges, trading houses, hospitals, preceptories and monasteries across Europe; very learned folk call such meeting places crays.
A typical lodge holds three or four cabals; the first tends to everyday business and relations with neighbors, and its leading adept, the magistrate, oversees every adept there.
A lodge begins as a communal society under a charter, and cabals that enjoy its shelter are expected to run errands, investigations or trade to keep it safe and prosperous.

title: The Maximi
summary: The leaders of the Daedalean Conventions.

claims.text: The Celestial Masters follow one Maximus, the Ksirafai admit to none, and each of the other five Conventions follows two Maximi, by custom one man and one woman.

title: Guilds of the Conventions
summary: The inner guilds and houses within each Daedalean Convention.

claims.text: Artificers include the Forgers or Vulcans, Bright Lions, Pythagorai and Mauls; Gabrielites include the Illustrofaratores, Poenitenti and Venatores Maleficorum or Falcons.
The Celestial Masters gather in the houses of Prometheus, Daedalus, Helios and Selene; Craftmasons sort into guilds named for the Chalice, Coin, Level, Hemlock, Arrow, Chisel, Stone and Scroll.

The High Guild holds the Resplendent Axe, the Patrons Guild or Black Uncles, the Royal Griffin, the Sun Guild and the Rose Guild; the Cosians form the houses of Mandrake, Fire, Books, Knives and Olympus plus the Phylaxoi; Void Seekers include the Alexandrians, Odysseans, the Guild of Forge and Sail, the Order of the Grail, the League of St. Paul and the Herculinian Compact.

title: The Order and the Council
summary: What the Order of Reason does not do.

claims.text: The Order is not at endless war with the Council of Nine and has no plan to kill every Tradition mage in Europe.
Daedaleans judge sorcerers, witches and warlocks by deeds; a few mages have been corrupted by power, but that does not damn every path other than reason.
